questions.instruction: Which expression does not belong because it is not a perfect square trinomial?
questions.stem: Which expression does not belong because it is not a perfect square trinomial?

options.misconception: Perfect square: (n − 1/2)².
Perfect square: (n − 1/3)².
Perfect square: (n + 1/6)².

answer.explanation: B, C and D equal (n−1/2)², (n−1/3)² and (n+1/6)². For n²+n+c to be a perfect square c must be (1/2)² = 1/4, not 3/4, so A does not belong.
